fields.System.Title: FDN-2 — Database foundation
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

A database organised so that module ownership is visible, changes are versioned, and a
realistic warehouse exists to develop against.

Scope

In. Schema per module, migration tooling, seed data for a demo warehouse.

Out. Partitioning, replication, tuning. Those arrive when there is data volume to justify
them.

Design notes

One PostgreSQL schema per module. masterdata.product, inventory.stock_balance. Costs
nothing, makes ownership visible in every table name, and groups the tables if a module is ever
extracted.

No foreign keys across schemas. Store the ID and validate in code. This trades
database-enforced integrity for the ability to change one module without touching another —
which is why [INT-503](../../stories/INT/INT-503-orphaned-reservations-report.md) and the
orphan checks exist.

Seed data must be awkward. A product with no barcode, a location at exactly maximum
capacity, a blocked location holding stock. Clean seed data hides the bugs you most want to
find early.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Autogenerated migrations that quietly destroy data | [doc 08 §7](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
| Migrations untested at production scale | [doc 09 §11.5](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Seed data too clean to expose defects | [doc 10 §6](../../../docs/10-local-deployment.md) |
